Délka kroku (m). Kratší krok při stejném: Stride length (m). A shorter stride at the same pace = higher cadence, and vice versa. We look at the change against your norm in comparable conditions.
Doba kontaktu se zemí (ms) — jak dlouho: Ground contact time (ms) — how long the foot stays on the ground. Longer than your norm (at a comparable pace) suggests fatigue or loss of support.
Efektivní „plochý ekvivalent\" kilometrů: Effective “flat equivalent” kilometres over 7 days — distance adjusted for the energy cost of the gradient (Minetti). A hilly run costs more than the same distance on the flat, so this number is higher than the real km on varied terrain. For a jump in load the terrain cost is counted separately: climbing by energy cost, descending by eccentric load — a steep descent costs less energy but loads the legs more.
Klidový tep přes noc. Trvale zvýšený pro: Resting heart rate overnight. Staying above your norm = the body hasn't recovered (fatigue, stress, illness). A one-off spike doesn't matter; watch the trend.
Podíl doby kontaktu se zemí na celkové d: Share of ground contact time in the whole stride (duty factor). Lower tends to be a springier, more economical run. Judged against your norm at a comparable pace — a rise goes with fatigue.
Poměr vertikálního pohybu k délce kroku: Vertical movement relative to stride length (%). Lower = more economical, “flatter” running. We look at the shift against your norm at a comparable pace and terrain — getting worse is often a sign of fatigue in form.
Připraveno — nakolik už známe vaši normu: Ready — how well we already know your technique norm (number of comparable runs and days of history). While it is low, mechanics signals are better kept hidden so they don't mislead.
Variabilita tepové frekvence přes noc (m: Heart rate variability overnight (ms). Higher = better recovered. What matters is the deviation from YOUR norm (in per cent), not the absolute value — a clearer drop against your usual spread points to fatigue or an illness coming on.
